questions.question: How much does SignalArc cost?
questions.answer: The Developer plan is free for one user. Startup begins at $49 per month and includes five users, 50 GB of monthly log ingestion, and 30 days of searchable log retention.

questions.question: Can I try paid features before subscribing?
questions.answer: Yes. New workspaces receive a 14-day Startup trial without requiring a credit card.

questions.question: Where is SignalArc data stored?
questions.answer: Developer and Startup data is stored in the United States. Enterprise customers can request the European Union region during contracting.

questions.question: Does SignalArc publish a SOC 2 report?
questions.answer: SignalArc is fictional and has no real compliance report. In a production course project, replace this answer only after the company can provide the report through a documented trust process.

questions.question: Can I delete telemetry before its retention period ends?
questions.answer: Yes. Workspace owners can delete a project and its associated telemetry from project settings. Deletion begins immediately and backup removal completes within 30 days.

questions.question: Does SignalArc support Next.js?
questions.answer: Yes. SignalArc supports browser and server errors, structured logs, and OpenTelemetry traces from Next.js applications. Source-map uploads require a CI step.

questions.question: Which alert destinations are supported?
questions.answer: SignalArc routes alerts to Slack, email, generic webhooks, and SignalArc on-call schedules. It does not provide voice-call escalation.

questions.question: Can I send OpenTelemetry data?
questions.answer: Yes. Startup and Enterprise plans accept OTLP traces over HTTPS. Metrics ingestion is not included in the course project.

questions.question: What support is included?
questions.answer: Developer includes community support. Startup includes email support on business days. Enterprise response targets are defined in the signed agreement.

questions.question: What should I include in a technical support request?
questions.answer: Include the framework and version, affected event ID, release identifier, timestamps, and relevant logs with tokens and personal data removed.
